Roman Alexeev was born on December 21, 1991, in Moscow, Russia. His early education took place at gymnasium № 534, where he demonstrated a keen interest in writing and storytelling. As a result, Roman's parents encouraged his curiosity by enrolling him in the Lomonosov Moscow State University's Journalism faculty upon completion of secondary school.

During his university years, Alexeev developed a passion for investigative journalism, which eventually led to his first internship at 'Vedomosti' journal. The experience left an indelible mark on him, and he went on to become an associate editor at the same publication, where he worked tirelessly to uncover hidden truths and shed light on the intricacies of Russian society.

Roman's personal life was marked by a strong desire for independence and self-reliance. He maintained a tight-knit circle of close friends, with whom he shared deep conversations about philosophy, literature, and the human condition. His preference for a solitary existence allowed him to cultivate his introspective nature and maintain a sense of emotional equilibrium.

Despite his natural talent for building relationships and his outgoing demeanor in professional settings, Roman struggled with forming long-term romantic connections. He valued his personal freedom above all else and chose to preserve his autonomy by maintaining a platonic status quo in his social life. His calmness, observational nature, and resourcefulness proved invaluable in navigating complex situations without becoming fully invested.

Over the years, Alexeev received recognition for his exceptional journalistic skills, including several notable awards for investigative reporting. His residence remained at 36 Taganskaya ul., Moscow, where he lived a relatively private life, often lost in thought as he pondered the intricacies of human nature and the world around him.

Throughout his life, Roman Alexeev continued to evolve as a writer, always pushing the boundaries of storytelling and truth-telling. His writing style, though introspective, conveyed an air of calmness and authority that commanded respect from those who followed his work.
